comment: Seven of the ten knobs share one helper, knobCV, which adds a fifth of the jack's voltage to the knob and clamps to 0..1, so ±5V covers the whole knob (src/scando.cpp:125-131). The in lvl knob has no jack of its own. The update rate is 500Hz times 16 raised to the knob, which is 500Hz to 8000Hz. Damping runs from 0.006 down to -0.0008, so the top of the knob feeds a little energy back in rather than removing it, which is why it approaches self-oscillation. A faint broadband noise rides along with strength only, so the string is exactly silent when strength is at zero. The technique is credited to Verplank, Mathews and Shaw at Interval Research, 1998 to 2000. The panel prints scando, fine, freq, shape, mass, stiff, strength, center, damp, rate, in lvl, excite, exc, inj, and the seven CV jack names, with v/oct and out at the bottom.
